senses.title: Attractive to look at

senses.example: She wore a pretty dress to the party.

senses.whyCN: 意为悦目的形容词弱化为程度副词：pretty good 就是好到让人满意。

senses.title: To dress up in a pleasing way
senses.definition: To dress up in a pleasing way
senses.example: She prettied herself up for the photo.
senses.why: The adjective took a verb ending; to pretty oneself is to make oneself look pleasing.
senses.whyCN: 形容词加上动词词尾：pretty oneself 就是把自己收拾得悦目。

definition_en: making little or no noise, or a state of silence, or to make someone or something silent
core_image: 深夜的教室只亮着一盏台灯，笔尖落在纸上几乎没有声音
scene: 深夜的教室里只亮着一盏台灯，笔尖落纸几乎没有声音。Please keep quiet during the exam.

senses.title: Making little or no noise
senses.definition: Making little or no noise
senses.example: Please keep quiet during the exam.
senses.why: Quiet came from Latin quietus, at rest; the word first marked a place free from disturbance.

senses.exampleCN: 屋里那份安静让我意外。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun naming the stillness itself, the rest that quietus described.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为名词，指宁静本身，也就是 quietus 所说的安歇。

senses.title: To make someone or something silent
senses.definition: To make someone or something silent
senses.example: She quieted the crying baby.
senses.exampleCN: 她把哭闹的婴儿哄静了。
senses.why: From the adjective came the verb: to quiet a room is to bring it to rest.
senses.whyCN: 由形容词生出动词：quiet 一间屋子就是让它安歇下来。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the word's real partners: its fixed phrase, its family, its recorded origin and its closest field.

normal.en: The fixed phrase 'a class schedule' gives the word one clear home.

abstract.en: Picture a class schedule pinned to the wall, several time slots circled in red, then let the picture change size until it covers both the everyday object and the figurative use.

root: 经古法语源自拉丁语 schedula（小纸片），原指写着时刻的纸条；由名词时间表转为动词，指把事情排进表里。

sensesIntro.en: Schedule means a plan that lists times for events, and as a verb it means to arrange for something to happen at a time.
sensesIntro.cn: schedule 指列出各项活动时间的表；作动词指把某事安排在规定的时间。
